faq.a: Ultraviolet light is light with shorter waves than violet, so our eyes cannot see it. It carries more energy than visible light, which is why it can damage skin and eyes.

faq.q: What does the ozone layer do?
faq.a: The ozone layer is a layer of ozone gas about 15 to 35 kilometres up. It absorbs all UV-C and most UV-B from the Sun, protecting life on the ground.
asks: Why is the ozone layer important?

faq.q: Can you get sunburnt on a cloudy day?
faq.a: Yes. Up to about 80 percent of UV can pass through light cloud, so you can burn even when it does not feel hot. Heat comes from infrared, not UV.
asks: Why did I burn when it was not sunny?

faq.a: Sunscreen contains ingredients that absorb UV or reflect it before it reaches your skin cells. The SPF number shows how well it protects against the UV-B that causes burning.
asks: Why should I wear sun cream?

faq.a: When UV hits skin, cells make more melanin, a brown pigment that absorbs UV. A tan is a sign the skin has already been damaged and is trying to protect itself.

facts: UV-C is completely absorbed by ozone and oxygen high in the atmosphere, and most UV-B is absorbed by the ozone layer.
The World Health Organization notes that up to 80 percent of UV radiation can pass through light cloud.
Sunburn redness usually appears a few hours after exposure and peaks about a day later.
